message.content:
What is true is that the quarter ended 2026-07-31 was the strongest on record, with revenue of $1.85 billion, up 36.54% from a year earlier, net income of $397 million, up 107.85%, and earnings per share of 2.82 against an estimate of 2.16 for a surprise of 30.56% [D1]. Gross margin was 65.87% and net margin was 21.51%, and earnings per share grew 63.95% on the year-earlier quarter [D1]. Management guided the fourth fiscal quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, a midpoint equal to growth of 37%, and to earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on 172 million diluted shares [D1]. The shares trade in an uptrend at a close of 333.42, above the 20-day average of 330.47, the 50-day average of 326.21 and the 200-day average of 289.31, with a 14-day relative strength index of 54.21 and a 14-day average true range of 11.05 [D1].

What the market is arguing about is the gap between that result and the price, since the shares fell 6.32% in the session of 2026-08-19 that followed the release of 2026-08-18 and the earlier release of 2026-05-19 was followed by a fall of 0.59% in the session of 2026-05-20 even though that quarter beat by 23.71% [D2]. The bulls' case is that the fourth-quarter revenue range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and the earnings per share range of $3.34 to $3.40 sit above what the market had been modelling, and that the demand behind them comes from artificial intelligence infrastructure spending, which lifted orders well beyond expectations [D2]. The bears' case is that the growth is already in the price, with a trailing price to earnings of 45.89 against a forward price to earnings of 20.66 [D5], and that management named supply rather than demand as the binding constraint, saying the supply environment is less flexible today than a year ago and that the supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. Management also cautioned that the one-time tariff impacts this year will not repeat, which raises the comparison bar for future profitability [D4].

The plan is therefore to let the trend and the guidance carry the position while supply decides the pace, holding while the close stays above the 50-day average of 326.21 and requiring the next report to deliver revenue at or above $1.93 billion and earnings per share at or above $3.34 before adding [D1]. The immediate resistance stands at 366.41 with a strength of 3, and immediate support runs from 332.78 to 300.87 with a strength of 59, so the downside levels are the ones that define the risk to the position [D1]. Session volume of 1.02 million compares with a 20-day average of 1.42 million, so the advance is not being carried by exceptional participation [D1]. The next dated event is not on file, and the swing to watch is the language on supply, which management said would govern the conversion of demand into revenue for the next several quarters [D3].
